title: Ombre fade pullover
excerpt: A drop-shoulder pullover in dk yarn that fades from a deep base colour at the hem through several intermediate shades to a pale tone at the shoulder. Each shade band is worked in plain dc rows. Graded XS to 3XL.
sourceNotes: Ombre gradient pullovers in dk weight are a popular beginner colour-sequence garment project.

glossaryTerms.definition: A section of rows worked in a single shade before transitioning to the next shade. In this pullover, each band is 8 rows tall. Using five shades of the same hue from dark to light produces a smooth step-by-step gradient across the body.
The point at which one shade band ends and the next begins. Completing the last stitch of the outgoing shade by drawing through the new shade colour keeps the transition line clean and horizontal.

crochet.gaugeText: 18 dc x 20 rows = 10 x 10 cm in dk on a 4 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Graded XS to 3XL. Size M: 104.4 cm bust.

content.text: Work all pieces in five equal
, starting with the darkest shade at the hem and ending with the palest at the shoulder. Use a
join at each band boundary. The sleeve follows the same shade sequence from cuff to shoulder, so the gradient reads consistently across the assembled garment. Seam each piece after completing it.
Size M: 188 sts wide, 81.7 cm body. Each band approx 16 cm tall. Sleeve 63.3 cm.
Chain 190. Work 5 shade bands in sequence, each approx 16 cm tall. Shape neck on front. Seam shoulders.
Chain 72. Work same 5-shade sequence from cuff upward, increasing each end every 4 rows for 63.3 cm total.
Seam sides. Work 2 rounds dc around neck in shade 5.
The colour field cardigan uses large rectangular colour zones across the body for a bold, graphic colourwork effect.

Work front panel the same as back, shaping a shallow neckline over the final 21 rows.
Work each sleeve: cast on 62, increase evenly to 124 over 125 rows.
Sew shoulder seams leaving a 41cm gap for the neckline.
Lay each sleeve flat across the open armhole and sew in place along the straight edge.
Sew side seams and underarm seams in one continuous line.
Pick up 74 stitches around the neckline and work neck trim. Weave in ends and block.
